recipes.name: Spicy Sweet Potato and Coconut Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (2 inch) piece fresh ginger root, thinly sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Place sweet potatoes directly onto the rack in the preheated oven and bake until tender enough to easily pierce with a fork, about 45 minutes. Remove from the oven and allow to cool.

While the potatoes are cooling, heat oil in a large saucepan or soup pot over medium heat. Add onion and ginger; cook and stir until tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in curry paste and heat for 1 minute, then whisk in vegetable broth and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, remove the skins from the sweet potatoes and cut the flesh into bite-sized chunks.

Add sweet potatoes to the soup and cook until they soak up the flavor, about 5 minutes. Stir in lemon juice and season with salt. Ladle into bowls and garnish with a drizzle of sesame oil and a little bit of cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Sweet Potato and Coconut Soup
raw_recipe.description: This smooth sweet potato soup with coconut milk and curry paste is easy to make and tastes great, delivering delicious Asian flavors in every spoonful.

review.reviewBody: EXCELLENT flavor! Fast supper technique: Put up broth to boil, (I used chicken rather than vegetable) peel the sweet potatoes, chunk them up into the broth, chunk up the onion and add to the broth. Substitution for curry paste and fresh ginger: 1 t chili powder, 1 t cumin, 1 t ginger, and 1 T curry powder. Once the potatoes were cooked, puree in the blender with the lemon juice and then pour back into pan and add the coconut milk, chopped cilantro & sesame oil. I skipped the salt. VERY tasty and quick! Garnished with a seasoned sour cream/yogurt blend and we can hardly wait to have leftovers tomorrow night!
Wow! Sooo yummy! The lemon tastes fantastic in it! Not spicy though - will add spicy peppers next time. I microwave the sweet potato to make it even easier. This is my go -to soup. Love it.
Baked sweet potatoes in microwave and then peeled and cubed. Off of cooktop, blended with immersion blender and then added lemon juice. Tasty.

Four stars as written, but my daughter and I thought the flavor was too subtle until we made the following changes: boiled the sweet potatoes as a time saver, thinned it out a little with more vegetable broth, doubled the curry paste (still could have used a little more heat), added the juice from 1/2 a lime. We also blended the finished soup right in the pot with an immersion blender. With the drizzle of sesame oil upon plating, we also sprinkled some sliced green onions (no cilantro on hand). It looked very elegant and tasted wonderful with these small changes.

Yummy! I made it in the crockpot (everything but the coconut milk, cilantro and sesame oil), put through the blender after cooking, and then stirred in the coconut milk at the end and garnished with cilantro and oil. I also used half vegetable broth / half chicken stock because that's what I had. I had an amazing Thai soup at a restaurant in Atlanta, and this tasted REALLY close to it!

I made this in an instant pot. I sautéed the onions and then stirred In the curry paste and ginger paste (rather than minced ginger). Added the peeled cut sweet potatoes - about 3/4”-1” - and 3 cups broth and 1 tsp. soy sauce. Cooked at high pressure for 5 minutes, then quick release. After the QR, stirred in light coconut milk and lemon/lime juice.

I'm not even going to pretend that I followed this recipe. I used it as a guide for the flavor profile and it was delicious. The first change I made gave the sweet potato a more roasted flavor since I sliced it thin (1/4-1/2 inch slices) and roasted it in a hot oven with olive oil and salt and pepper. Then, I sauted grated ginger and sliced onion in a mix of coconut oil and sesame oil. After they were tender, I added curry powder (probably about a tablespoon) and continued to cook the mixture until it was fragrant. Then, I added the sweet potatoes, vegetable broth, and coconut milk. After seasoning with salt and pepper, I added a hit of lemon juice. After simmering a while, I pureed the soup and served it with fresh cilantro, sour cream, and toasted pepitas. Yummy!

The recipe does not specify pureeing the soup, but the picture looks like it was pureed. I did not bake the sweet potatoes first; rather peeled and cubed them and sauteed after the onions, adding some vegetarian broth. Fresh ginger gives it a good bite. Did not have curry paste but substituted red chili, coriander, curry powder. Used a drizzle of spicy red chili tahini on the top, under the chopped fresh cilantro. Served to guests, every drop was disappeared!
I love the simplicity of a recipe that is so flavorful. I microwaved the sweet potatoes to save time and did use an immersion blender to make it smooth. We make this often!

I did not use my oven but peeled and chopped the sweet potato and cooked with some oil in a soup pot till slightly caramelized, then added onion etc.. We enjoyed the soup without the sesame and cilantro. I found the sesame oil much to strong a flavor and aroma. Served with garlic cheese flat bread from this site.

Wow. This soup is amazing. If you can please use the fresh ginger and red curry paste; I believe they make this dish. The only ingred. I changed was chicken broth. I microwaved the sweet potatoes and they peeled easily. After soup was done I took about 3/4 of it and blended it in blender. This left just a few pieces for texture but mostly a beautful creamy red soup. Thanks Lynn!
This soup was so easy to make and it is absolutely delicious. I didn’t have fresh ginger on hand so I used ground ginger. I will definitely make it again.
Cannot believe how good this was! My entire family of carnivores was begging for more!
Loved it! I doubled the red curry for more flavor & mashed half the sweet potatoes to thicken. Served with whole foods super grains blend & black beans.

I was very skeptical, mainly because I've had bad luck using curry...but this soup is VERY TASTY. After reading other reviews, I substituted chicken broth (homemade) vs. vegetable broth. Adding the sesame oil and cilantro on top after serving is definitely a must, it adds so much flavor. I would like to add some more spice, as i prefer a little bit of heat. My husband said if he read this on a restaurant menu, he would never order it, but now after he's tasted it, he will...maybe. But overall, very tasty. Thanks Lynn!!!

I’m not really sure how the calories came out to 306 cal per serving for this but I have done my own scanning of each ingredient and the calories per serving are 160. Not sure why everybody’s soups are looking like purées however. I followed the directions to the letter and minors showing up with chunks of sweet potato and a vegetable broth with red curry paste etc. The flavors are good but I’m not sure why everybody’s submitting pictures with the soup puréed. I too prefer a purée but I was trying to make it as per the recipe. Definitely not spicy! I used Thai spice red curry paste and I almost think it could’ve used twice the amount of curry to even make that spice hit.
Yum yum
Honestly this was delicious, I used ground ginger instead of fresh but otherwise followed exactly and it was so easy and tasted amazing!
Good flavor. I used chicken broth instead of vegetable broth.

A friend gifted us with about 15 lbs of sweet potatoes this summer, and I was scrambling for recipes. This one came up, I had everything I needed to make it, and just went ahead! Absolutely delicious and satisfying. I doubled the red curry paste, because we like it spicy. Other than that, this recipe really rocked it for us!
